title: Proposed NM India-only API contracts — not installed routes
$comment: Structural planning contract. x-commands is the command catalogue; request/response refs resolve locally. JSON Schema validates shape, not legal judgment, permissions, hashes, state transition or implementation. Those need the named served-path AC proof.
x-scope: Confidential target profile; catalogue completion does not install routes. Existing /api routes retain their compatibility contract unless explicitly adopted. D-041 explicitly adopts public email/password plus separate invited registration and neutral public authentication failures; it does not adopt confidential factor routes or confer deployment approval.
x-example-policy: Synthetic shape witnesses only, never credentials or measured runtime results. Every command has positive and negative request and response examples. Cross-record semantic refusals are separate obligations.

x-common-rules.identity: principal_id, tenant_id, role, assurance, access epoch and timestamps come only from validated server context. Route/query IDs are untrusted resource claims. No body actor override.
x-common-rules.secret_handling: Passwords, invitation/recovery codes, provider proof, CSRF and session secrets never enter traces, command response cache or evidence. Persist keyed request digest, not credential-bearing request; rotate digest keys independently. Secret responses are delivered once and never replayed.
x-common-rules.transport: HTTPS confidential deployment, same-origin CSRF-protected POST, HttpOnly Secure SameSite session cookies. GET has empty body. Query objects serialize as canonical percent-encoded JSON for the structured locator only; scalar query members use ordinary encoding.
x-common-rules.header_matching: HTTP field names case-insensitive, normalised to declared case before schema validation. Idempotency-Key UUID4. If-Match is a strong ETag string such as "v7"; never wildcard. Body/query/path additional fields are refused.
x-common-rules.idempotency: Every POST allocates accepted_command scoped by server tenant/principal/operation/Idempotency-Key and keyed canonical semantic request digest. Include path/body/If-Match; exclude replaceable CSRF and transport headers. Same key + different intent =>409. Check recognised replay before stale-version precondition; reauthorise even on replay. At least 30 days non-secret retry receipt for application commands; external action deduplication retained for action lifecycle. Secret/auth receipts follow scoped short-lived policy and never replay secrets.
x-common-rules.optimistic_concurrency: If-Match names target aggregate in route, except set-commission/begin-upload/submit-turn/start-research/create-action-proposal/create-handover/close-matter/reopen-matter where it names matter; publish-corpus names corpus activation epoch; rotation names recovery generation. Commands with additional expected_matter_version require both to match atomically. First corpus publication alone permits If-Match="v0" with expected_active_manifest_id=null; later publication requires an existing active ID and positive epoch.
x-common-rules.read_consistency: Read under current policy and a consistent snapshot; return exact resource version in data and ETag on versioned resources. Cursor binds actor/workspace/policy/filter/snapshot; no total-count exposure from inaccessible rows.
x-common-rules.mutation_commit: Permission + version check + canonical writes + operation result + outbox + minimal audit in one DB transaction. No provider/model call under transaction. Saved acknowledgment follows commit. A no-save refusal must leave no legal/canonical effect.
x-common-rules.time: All instants UTC RFC3339; legal calendar dates remain date-only plus basis. Server checks date ranges/start-end ordering, expiry and policy maxima; client review flag never substitutes for an attributable approved review.
x-common-rules.exceptions: Error.code and fixed http_status/outcome/retry combinations are the Error schema. Messages are plain safe text; no SQL, stack, credentials, raw provider payload, legal material or cross-tenant existence. Retry-After seconds required on429/503 when retry is after_delay.
x-common-rules.async_completion: 202 acknowledges durable intent/input, never completion or legal quality. Only get-operation/get-job expose progress; completed legal output requires release receipt and current dependencies. Unknown external effect requires reconciliation.
x-common-rules.bounds: Schema limits are absolute transport ceilings, not an advertised capability. Active reviewed capability/purpose/tenant budget may be lower; no silently larger provider-bound payload. Upload uses sequential1MiB decoded chunks; binary download verifies bytes and can abort on revocation.
x-common-rules.auth_boundary: Proposed confidential login begins assurance challenge, never issues privileged password-only session. Prototype /api login remains legacy until target adoption. Factor-provider-specific protocol must be pinned and verified by approved bridge; no arbitrary redirect, issuer or custom authenticator implementation. reauthenticate-session supplies a local-password proof only in the controlled local profile; confidential use refuses it. Both paths use the same purpose/generation-bound proof consumer.
x-common-rules.catalogue_change: Adding or changing a command requires an existing exact owner_ac, local closed schemas, positive and negative witnesses, semantic refusal, transition owner and compatible route decision. Catalogue completion is not runtime completion.

email.description: Public signup only; normalised by the identity owner. This is a login handle, not proof of mailbox possession or professional qualification. Forbidden when an invitation fixes identity.

x-commands.authorization: Public email/password/confirmation creates only a server-owned actor-private account/workspace; no invitation or professional approval is required for signup or subsequent owned-workspace/new/reopen use. Optional single-use expiring invitation is a separate password-only lane fixing the exact principal and firm workspace. Neither lane accepts profile/role/approval/workspace injection or verifies mailbox possession/professional qualification. Same-origin CSRF bootstrap and bounded rate controls precede expensive work; credential owner checks password equality/policy. Does not sign in.
transitions: new canonical email + accepted credential offer -> one personal principal + actor-private workspace + hashed recovery set; no professional approval is created
valid_unspent_invitation + password-only offer -> consumed + exact invited principal/workspace + hashed recovery set atomically; invalid invitation cannot fall through into public registration
duplicate/concurrent canonical identity -> no credential replacement, membership change, role grant or second secret delivery
x-commands.retry: Secret set is delivered once, never stored in command response cache or logs. Replay returns SECRET_ALREADY_DELIVERED; use sign-in/recovery procedure, not a second enrolment.
x-commands.semantic_refusal: Body principal_id, firm/workspace, role or verification/approval injection is schema-invalid. Public email and invited identity cannot be mixed. Concurrent public/invited claims for one canonical account yield at most one registration and never replace the existing credential. Public failures disclose no private roster/workspace content.
